sanskrit: ṛtāvānaṃ vaiśvānaram ṛtasya jyotiṣas patim | ajasraṃ gharmam īmahe ||
english: We implore Vaiśvānara, the possessor of cosmic order, the lord of the light of truth — the unceasing, blazing heat.

sanskrit: sa idaṃ prati paprathad yajñasya svar uttiran | ṛtūn ut sṛjate vaśī ||
english: He spread this forth, lifting up the heavenly light of sacrifice; the self-willed one releases the seasons.

sanskrit: agniḥ priyeṣu dhāmasu kāmo bhūtasya bhavyasya | samrāḍ eko vi rājati ||
english: Agni in his beloved abodes, the desire of all that has been and all that shall be — the sole sovereign shines resplendent.

sanskrit: pari dyām iva sūryo ahīnāṃ janim āgamam | rātrī jagad ivānyad dhaṃsād avārīr imaṃ viṣam ||
english: As the sun circles the sky, I have come to the birth-place of the serpents; as the night sweeps aside the other world, so ward off this poison.

sanskrit: yad brahmabhir yad ṛṣibhir yad devair uditaṃ purā | yad bhūtaṃ bhavyam āsanvat tena te vāraye viṣam ||
english: By what was uttered in ancient times by the brahmin-priests, by the seers, by the gods — by whatever existed and shall come to be — with that I ward off your poison.

sanskrit: madhunāpṛkṣi nadyaḥ parvatā girayo madhu | madhu paruṣṇī śīpālā śam āsne astu śaṃ hṛde ||
english: The rivers are mingled with honey; the mountains and hills are honey; sweet is the Paruṣṇī, sweet the water-plants — may there be ease for the face, ease for the heart.

sanskrit: yatheyam urvī pṛthivī dādhāra viṣṭhitaṃ jagat | evā te dhriyatāṃ garbho anu sūtuṃ savitave ||
english: As this broad earth has borne the established world, so may your embryo be held firm, to be brought forth for the Vivifier.

sanskrit: (…) dādhāremān vanaspatīn | (…) ||
english: [Lacuna] ... may these forest-lords be borne ... [Lacuna].

sanskrit: yatheyam urvī pṛthivī dādhāra parvatān apaḥ | evā te dhriyatāṃ garbho anu sūtuṃ suvitave ||
english: As this broad earth has borne the mountains and the waters, so may your embryo be held firm, to be brought forth for well-being.

sanskrit: sasruṣīs tad apaso divā naktaṃ ca sasruṣīḥ | vareṇyakratur aham apo devīr upa bruve ||
english: Flowing by day and flowing by night — I, of excellent resolve, call upon you, divine waters, you who flow on.

sanskrit: oktā āpaḥ karmaṇyā muñcantv itaḥ praṇītaye | sadyo bhavantv etave ||
english: May the waters, invoked, the active ones, release from here for guidance — may they immediately come to pass.

sanskrit: devasya savituḥ save karma kṛṇvanti mānuṣāḥ | śaṃ no bhavantv apa oṣadhīr imāḥ ||
english: At the impulsion of the divine Savitṛ, human beings perform their work — may these waters and herbs be propitious to us.

sanskrit: śatasya te dhamanīnāṃ sahasrasya hirāṇām | asthur in madhyamā yāḥ sākam antā araṃsata ||
english: Of your hundred channels and of your thousand veins, those that stand in the middle — together they have come to rest at the extremities.

sanskrit: pari vaḥ sikatāmayīr dhanūs tiraś cid asthiran | tiṣṭhatelayatā su kam ||
english: Around you the sand-made bows stood firm even crosswise; stand still, trembling lightly, be at peace.

sanskrit: amūr yā yanti jāmayaḥ sarvā lohitavāsasaḥ | abhrātara iva yoṣās tiṣṭhanti hatavarcasaḥ ||
english: Those kinswomen who go yonder, all clad in red — like women without brothers they stand, their splendor struck down.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhāvare tiṣṭha para uta tvaṃ tiṣṭha madhyame | kaṇiṣṭhikā ca tiṣṭhāti tiṣṭhād id dhamanir mahī ||
english: Stand still, O lower one; stand still, O upper one; and you too stand still, O middle one; may the little finger also stand still; may the great vein stand still.

sanskrit: namo devavadhebhyo namo rājavadhebhyaḥ | atho ye viśyānāṃ vadhās tebhyo mṛtyo namāṃsi te ||
english: Homage to the deaths inflicted by gods, homage to the deaths inflicted by kings; and those deaths that belong to the common folk — to them, O Death, I offer you reverence.

sanskrit: namas te adhivākāya parāvākāya te namaḥ | sumatyai mṛtyo te namo durmatyai ta idaṃ namaḥ ||
english: Homage to you in your aspect of pronouncing over, homage to you in your aspect of pronouncing away; O Death, homage to your benevolent thought, and to your malevolent thought this homage.

sanskrit: namas te yātudhānebhyo namas te bheṣajebhyaḥ | mūlebhyo mṛtyo te namo brāhmaṇebhya idaṃ namaḥ ||
english: Homage to your sorcerers, homage to your remedies; O Death, homage to your roots, and to the brahmin-priests this homage.

sanskrit: nava ca yā navatiś ca saṃyanti manyā abhi | itas tāḥ sarvā naśyantu vākā apacitām iva ||
english: The nine and the ninety that come together towards the neck — may all of them vanish from here, like the growths of the apacit disease.

sanskrit: sapta ca yāḥ saptatiś ca saṃyanti skandhyā abhi | (itas tāḥ sarvā naśyantu vākā apacitām iva) ||
english: The seven and the seventy that come together towards the shoulders — may all of them vanish from here, like the growths of the apacit disease.

sanskrit: pañca ca yāḥ pañcāśac ca saṃyanti graivyā abhi | itas tāḥ sarvā naśyantu vākā apacitām iva ||
english: The five and the fifty that come together towards the throat — may all of them vanish from here, like the growths of the apacit disease.

sanskrit: āvayo anāvayo rasas ta ugra āvayo | ā te karambham adīmahi sa hi na tvam asi yas tvam ātmānam āvayaḥ ||
english: The devouring one, the non-devouring one — your essence, O fierce devourer; we have eaten your gruel — for you are indeed that one by which you have devoured yourself.

sanskrit: babhruś ca babhrukarṇaś ca nīlākalaśālā | śavaḥpaśya ||
english: The brown one and the brown-eared one, the blue-eared pot-lady — O Corpse-gazer.

sanskrit: tauvilike 'velayā- -avāyam ailava ailayīt | iha svām āhutiṃ juṣāṇo manasā svāhā ||
english: O Tauvilikā, with Avelā — one has devoured, Ailava has devoured; here, accepting your own oblation with mind — svāhā.

sanskrit: svāhā manasā yad idaṃ kṛṇomi yasyās ta āsañ juhomi ghore | eṣāṃ baddhānām avasarjanāya kam ||
english: Svāhā — with mind I make this offering; into her whose they were I pour it, O terrible one, for the releasing of these bound ones.

sanskrit: bhūmir iti tvābhipramanvate janā nirṛtir iti tvāhaṃ pari veda viśvataḥ | bhūte haviṣmaty asy eṣa te bhagas tena te vidheyaṃ svāhā ||
english: People think of you as Earth; I know you all around as Nirṛti, from every side; in truth you are rich in oblations — this is your portion, and through it service is to be rendered to you — svāhā.

sanskrit: evo ṣv asmat tvaṃ nirṛte viśvavāre ayasmayān pra mumugdhi pāśān | yamena tvaṃ yamyā saṃvidānā yo asmān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas tasmin tān pāśān prati muñca sarvān ||
english: So thus, O Nirṛti of all desirable things, release from us your iron bonds; you who are allied with Yama as his twin — the one who hates us and the one we hate, upon him cast all those bonds back.

sanskrit: uttamo asy oṣadhīnāṃ tava vṛkṣā upastayaḥ | upastir asmākaṃ bhūyād yo 'smām̐ abhidāsati ||
english: You are the highest among plants; the trees are your support. May there be support for us against the one who seeks to harm us.

sanskrit: sabandhuś cāsabandhuś ca yo 'smām̐ abhidāsati | sabandhūn sarvāṃs tīrtvā- -ahaṃ bhūyāsam uttamaḥ ||
english: Whether he who seeks to harm us has kinsmen or has no kinsmen — crossing beyond all those with kinsmen, may I become the highest.

sanskrit: yathā soma oṣadhīnām uttamaṃ havir ucyate | evā tvam iva vṛkṣāṇām ahaṃ bhūyāsam uttamaḥ ||
english: Just as Soma is called the highest oblation among plants, so — like you among trees — may I become the highest.

sanskrit: indrasya vacasā vayaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya ca | devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vācā yakṣmaṃ te vārayāmahe ||
english: By the word of Indra, of Mitra, and of Varuṇa, and by the word of all the gods, we ward off the disease from you.

sanskrit: yathā vṛtra imā āpas tastambha viśvadhā yatīḥ | evā te agninā yakṣmaṃ vaiśvānareṇa vāraye ||
english: Just as Vṛtra held back these waters striving to flow in every direction, so I ward off your disease with Agni Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa haviṣā- -abhi somaṃ mṛśāmasi | atrā ta indraḥ kevalīr viśo balihṛtas karat ||
english: With a firm oblation we anoint the firm Soma; here let Indra make the clans, the tribute-bearing ones, yours alone.

sanskrit: ā tvāhārṣam antar abhūr dhruvas tiṣṭhāvicācalat | viśas tvā sarvā ā yantu mā tvad rāṣṭram adhi bhraśat ||
english: I have brought you here; you have become present within, firm, standing unshaken; may all the clans come to you — let not the kingdom slip away from you.

sanskrit: ihaivaidhi māpa cyoṣṭhāḥ parvata ivāvicācalat | indreha dhruvas tiṣṭha- -iha rāṣṭraṃ ni dhāraya ||
english: Be here, do not go away, standing unshaken like a mountain; be firm here, O Indra — hold the kingdom firm here.

sanskrit: indra etam adīdharad dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa haviṣā | tasmai somo adhi bruvad ayaṃ ca brahmaṇaspatiḥ ||
english: Indra made this one firm with a firm oblation; in his favor Soma spoke out, and so did Brahmaṇaspati here.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ te devaḥ savitā dhruvaṃ devo bṛhaspatiḥ | dhruvaṃ ta indraś cāgniś ca rāṣṭraṃ dhārayatāṃ dhruvam ||
english: May the divine Savitṛ hold your realm firm, may divine Bṛhaspati hold it firm; may Indra and Agni hold your realm, the unshaken, firmly in place.

sanskrit: dhruvā dyaur dhruvā pṛthivī samudrāḥ parvatā dhruvāḥ | dhruvā ha dharmaṇā dhruvā dhruvo rājā viśām ayam ||
english: Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, firm are the oceans and the mountains; firm indeed by sacred law, firm — firm is this king of the clans.

sanskrit: vṛṣendrasya vṛṣā divo vṛṣā pṛthivyā ayam | vṛṣā viśvasya bhūtasya tvam ekavṛṣo bhava ||
english: The bull of Indra, the bull of the sky, the bull of the earth is this one; bull of all that exists — become the sole bull.

sanskrit: samudra īśe sravatām agniḥ pṛthivyā vaśī | sūryo nakṣatrāṇām īśe tvam (…) ||
english: The ocean rules over the flowing waters; Agni is the lord of the earth; the Sun rules over the constellations; you [rule over ...] [Lacuna].

sanskrit: samrāḍ asy asurāṇāṃ kakun manuṣyāṇām | devānām ardhabhāg asi tvam ekavṛṣo bhava ||
english: You are the sovereign of the Asuras, the chief among human beings; you are a half-sharer among the gods — become the sole bull.

sanskrit: pari vartmāny eṣām indraḥ pūṣā ca sasratuḥ | muhyantv adyāmūḥ senā amitrāṇāṃ parastarām ||
english: Indra and Pūṣan have run around the paths of these enemies; may those armies of the foes yonder be confused today and henceforth.

sanskrit: mugdhā amitrāś caranta- -aśīrṣāṇa ivāhayaḥ | athaiṣām agniruddhānām indro hantu varaṃ-varam ||
english: Bewildered, may the foes wander like headless serpents; then, of these whose fire is blocked, let Indra smite the best one after another.

sanskrit: aiṣu nahya vṛṣājinaṃ hariṇasya bhiyaṃ kṛdhi | parāṅ amitra eṣatv arvācī gaur upeṣatu ||
english: Bind the bull's hide upon these enemies; strike terror as of the antelope into them; may the foe rush away in retreat, and may the cow approach toward us.
